facts.fact: The DNEC's head of digitalisation, presenting on 18 July 2026, describes the birth chain as paper: community health workers fill village notebooks, the declaration agent sends slip no. 2 from the declaration centre to the civil status centre, where the officer draws up the act; he calls it a paper community model, lists availability of registers among the difficulties, and names complete digitalisation of the system as a priority, the digital transformation being still incomplete.

note: The document also gives registration rates of 89.5% births, 50% deaths and 20% marriages, which are shares of events and not of offices; the planned move to electronic birth notification and real-time data transmission is a stated perspective, with no date or system named.
